title: Protocol for Monitoring DNA-Triggered cGAS/STING Signaling in Mammalian Cells and Mice
protocol: Split sub-confluent EA.hy926 cells into 24-well plates (∼ 5 × 10^4 cells/well).
Leave untreated cells for 8–10 hours to reach ∼60%–70% confluence upon transfection.
Mix desired amounts of ISD90 or 2′,3′-cGAMP with P3000 in a 1:2 ratio in OPTI-MEM medium.
For example, mix 2.5 μg ISD90 with 5 μL P3000 in 65 μL OPTI-MEM medium.
Mix lipofectamine 3000 with OPTI-MEM medium at a 1:3 ratio for ISD90/2′,3′-cGAMP to lipofectamine 3000.
For example, mix 5 μL lipofectamine 3000 with 65 μL OPTI-MEM medium.
Mix DNA complex and lipid complex together and vortex at medium speed.
Leave the mixture at room temperature (∼25°C) for 15 minutes.
Carefully and slowly drop the mixture onto cells.
Wash cells with sterile PBS after 5–6 h post transfection.
Culture cells in DMEM medium supplemented with 10% FBS and antibiotics until cell collection is required for analysis.
Wash cells with 1× PBS at desired time periods post transfection.
Lysate cells using EBC buffer or Triton X-100 buffer supplemented with protease inhibitors and phosphatase inhibitors.
Incubate cell lysates at 4°C for 10 minutes with gentle rotation.
Centrifuge the samples in an Eppendorf 5424R centrifuge at 4°C for 10 minutes at maximum speed to remove debris.
Transfer supernatants to a new tube and store as whole cell lysates (WCL).
Mix 1 μL of WCL with 1 mL of 1:5 diluted Bradford protein assay reagent.
Determine protein concentrations by Nanodrop OneC.
Establish a standard curve using BSA at concentrations of 1, 3, 6, and 9 μg/μL.
Add 1/3 volume of 3× SDS sample buffer into WCL and boil samples at 95°C for 10 min.
Spin down samples briefly after boiling to collect evaporates.
Vortex samples before loading on 10% SDS-PAGE gels in SDS-PAGE running buffer.
Run SDS-PAGE gels at 128 V constant voltage for 70 min or until dye front reaches the bottom of the gel.
Assemble transfer sandwiches by positioning SDS-PAGE gel next to PVDF membrane per manufacturer instructions in transfer buffer.
Remove air bubbles from assembled transfer sandwiches with rollers purchased from Bio-Rad.
Insert transfer sandwiches into western blot transfer device in SDS-PAGE transfer buffer and cooling pad at 128 V for 2 h.
Block PVDF membranes with 5% non-fat milk in TBST buffer for 30 min on a Labnet shaker at room temperature (∼25°C).
Dilute primary antibodies in 5% non-fat milk to a 1:1,000 dilution and incubate with PVDF membranes at 4°C for 8–10 h with gentle shaking.
Wash PVDF membranes thoroughly with 1× TBST buffer with shaking on a Labnet shaker at room temperature (∼25°C) for 10 min and repeat four times.
Dilute HRP-conjugated secondary antibodies into 5% non-fat milk in TBST buffer at a 1:3,300 dilution.
Incubate PVDF membrane with diluted secondary antibodies for 1 hour at room temperature (∼25°C) with gentle shaking.
Wash PVDF membranes thoroughly with 1× TBST buffer for four times, each for 10 minutes at room temperature (∼25°C) with shaking on a shaker.
Incubate PVDF membranes with ECL reagents for 5 minutes at room temperature (∼25°C).
Image PVDF membranes using QUANT imager.
Extract total RNA using RNeasy mini kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Dissolve extracted RNA in DNase-free and RNase-free DEPC water.
Determine RNA concentrations by a spectrophotometer (Nanodrop OneC, Thermo Scientific).
Use iScriptTM Reverse Transcription Supermix for RT-qPCR to reversely transcribe mRNA into cDNA following manufacturer’s instructions.
A total of 1 μg RNA is used as the template in this step.
Mix iTaqTM universal SYBR Green Supermix with cDNA template (with a final amount of 500 ng), forward and reverse primers (500 nM of each primer) together in a 20 μL reaction volume.
Perform the PCR reaction on the ViiATM6 Real-Time PCR system with the settings as specified.
Reconstitute Capture Antibody with 0.5 mL PBS to the working concentration.
Dilute Capture Antibody reconstitution solution (480 μg/mL) with PBS without carrier protein to a working solution concentration of 4.00 μg/mL.
Coat high binding 96-well plate with Capture Antibody working solution (100 μL/well).
Cover the plate and incubate at 4°C for 8–10 h.
Aspirate wells after coating.
Wash wells three times with Wash Buffer (0.05% Tween-20 in PBS, pH 7.2–7.4, 400 μL/well).
Invert and tap the plate on clean paper towels to remove remaining Wash Buffer.
Block the plate with blocking solution (1% BSA in PBS, pH 7.2–7.4, 300 μL/well) for 1 hour at room temperature (∼25°C).
Reconstitute standard with 0.5 mL Reagent Diluent.
Dilute standard reconstitution solution to a working solution concentration of 500 pg/mL using Reagent Diluent.
Perform a seven-point standard curve by using 2-fold serial dilutions from 500 pg/mL.
Centrifuge culture media at top speed briefly to eliminate cell debris or dead cells.
Add 100 μL standard and centrifuge-cleared supernatant (mixed with Reagent Diluent) to designated wells.
Seal the plate and incubate for 2 h at room temperature (∼25°C).
Reconstitute Detection Antibody with 1 mL Reagent Diluent.
Dilute Detection Antibody reconstitution solution to a working solution concentration of 250 ng/mL using Reagent Diluent.
Add Detection Antibody working solution to each well (100 μL/well), seal the plate, and incubate for 2 h at room temperature (∼25°C).
Dilute Streptavidin-HRP with Reagent Diluent to a working solution concentration (a 40-fold dilution).
Add 100 μL Streptavidin-HRP working solution to each well.
Seal the plate and incubate in the dark for 30 min at room temperature (∼25°C).
Repeat step 12b in the preparation of plates.
Add 100 μL substrate solution to each well, seal the plate and incubate the plate in the dark for 20 min at room temperature (∼25°C).
Add 50 μL of Stop Solution to each well.
Measure absorbance with a microplate reader (BioTek Cytation 5) at 450 nm after adding Stop Solution.
Generate the standard curve (y axis: protein concentration, x axis: absorbance) with a 4-parameter algorithm using Excel.
Subtract background from the readings by using the blank samples and use the standard curve to calculate concentrations of samples.
Inject 100 μL of purified HSV-1 viruses (in PBS) with indicated pfu into indicated mice through tail vein injection.
Inject 100 μL of streptavidin nanoparticles into indicated mice through tail vein injection.
Euthanize mice using carbon dioxide for at least 4 min followed by cervical dislocation according to the approved IACUC protocol.
Collect blood by cardiac puncture immediately after mice are euthanized.
Store collected blood in clean sterile Eppendorf tubes.
Centrifuge the tube with collected blood for at least 15 min at 1,000 × g.
Pipette serum or plasma into a clean Eppendorf tube and attach label.
Avoid transferring red blood cells into the final tube.
Store serum at -80°C before ELISA to detect interferon and cytokines.
Harvest spleen and brain tissues after euthanasia.
Split harvested tissues into three sections.
Store tissue sections at -80°C before further analysis.
Extract RNA from the first aliquot using QIAGEN RNeasy Mini Kits following manufacturer's instructions.
Perform qRT-PCR to detect cellular gene expression at the RNA level.
Extract DNA from the second aliquot using QIAGEN DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kits following manufacturer’s instructions.
Perform qPCR on the extracted DNA to detect HSV-1 genome copy numbers.
Grind tissues in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube with a plastic pestle in lysis buffer (EBC buffer).
Extract proteins from the ground tissue for western blot analysis.
Conduct western blot analysis to detect cellular protein or HSV-1 viral protein expression levels.
